provenance: Lane split authored by the Stage-2 decision-agent (read-only; returns JSON in reply) and persisted by the orchestrator as the agent's returned detect-vs-hunt partition. Detection = seed complement of the agent's hunt set; validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup, and det-count reconciled against the agent's summary. All ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset. Per-technique rationale shows the Stage-1 detection-feasibility basis.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — valid-account abuse is detectable via impossible-travel, anomalous-logon and first-seen sign-in analytics on authentication logs
medium — malicious-attachment delivery is detectable via mail sandboxing and macro-content analysis at the gateway
medium — link-based spearphishing is detectable via URL detonation and proxy telemetry to newly-registered/lookalike domains
high — Office applications spawning script/child processes after macro enablement is a core, well-covered detectable behavior
medium — link clicks are detectable via URL-gateway and proxy logs; endpoint signal is indirect
high — script-block/module logging and suspicious PowerShell parenting are core, well-covered detections

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: high — cmd.exe execution with anomalous parents and command lines is visible in process-creation logs

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
detection_candidates.rationale: high — Office spawning script children via VBA macros is a strong, detectable process-lineage anomaly
high — scheduled-task creation is logged (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational) and highly detectable

detection_candidates.technique_name: Event Triggered Execution: Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — WMI permanent event-subscription creation is detectable via WMI-Activity logging and __EventFilter/__EventConsumer telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: high — Run-key value creation is directly detectable via registry-modification telemetry
high — brute-force patterns are detectable via failed-logon volume and lockout analytics on authentication logs
high — password spraying is detectable via many-accounts/few-passwords sign-in analytics and distributed failed-auth patterns (a signature HEXANE initial-access TTP)
medium — password-store access is detectable mainly via known-tool execution signatures and file-access to credential stores

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — access to browser Login Data / credential stores is detectable via file-access and known-tool telemetry
medium — ipconfig-style recon is common but suspicious within tight process-lineage context

detection_candidates.technique_name: System Network Configuration Discovery: Internet Connection Discovery
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — connectivity checks to well-known hosts are common; meaningful in process-lineage/beaconing context
medium — host-enumeration commands (net view, ping sweeps) are detectable in command-line logs but need baselining
medium — whoami/username enumeration is common; value is in process-lineage correlation
medium — netstat-style enumeration is common but meaningful in process-lineage context
medium — tasklist/Get-Process enumeration is common but meaningful in process-lineage context
medium — 'net localgroup' enumeration is directly observable in command-line logging
medium — systeminfo-style discovery is common; suspicious mainly in process-lineage context
medium — file/dir enumeration is common; meaningful when correlated in process lineage
medium — 'net user'/account enumeration is directly observable in command-line logs
high — 'net user /domain' and net group domain enumeration are directly observable in command-line logging
medium — software enumeration is detectable in script/command telemetry; needs baselining
medium — anomalous internal RDP sessions are detectable via logon type 10 (Event 4624) and network-flow analytics
medium — internal-origin phishing is detectable via mail-flow anomalies and unusual send patterns from compromised accounts
medium — archive creation of staged data is detectable via file-write and known-archiver process telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — archiver utilities used against staged directories are a detectable LOLBin/staging pattern
medium — HTTP C2 is detectable via proxy/beacon analytics and URI/JA3 anomalies but blends with normal web traffic

high — DNS tunneling is a strong detection surface: high query volume to a single domain, long/high-entropy subdomain labels, unusual TXT/A record patterns and non-resolver DNS destinations are all detectable in DNS logs (priority detection candidate for this actor)
medium — protocol tunneling is detectable via traffic-shape and entropy analytics on the carrier protocol (DNS), overlapping with the T1071.004 DNS-tunneling detection surface
medium — tool transfer over C2 is detectable via file-write-after-network telemetry and, where HTTP is used, download analytics
medium — encoded C2 content is detectable via encoding heuristics and entropy analysis where traffic is inspectable
medium — protocol-on-non-standard-port mismatches are detectable via netflow/firewall analytics
medium — obfuscated content is detectable via entropy/encoding heuristics and static signatures; needs supporting context

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Command Obfuscation
detection_candidates.rationale: high — obfuscated/encoded commands are detectable via script-block logging and encoding/entropy heuristics
medium — runtime decode routines are observable in script-block and command-line logging
medium — tampering with security tooling (service/registry/process changes) is detectable via service-state and registry-modification telemetry
medium — exfil over C2 blends with C2 traffic; detectable via outbound-volume/beacon anomalies and, for DNS, oversized/high-frequency query analytics

detection_candidates.technique_name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — uploads to cloud-storage endpoints are detectable via proxy/DLP telemetry and anomalous data-volume to cloud APIs
